title: Former Citibank Employee and Community  Support
description: A strong, competent, remarkable and proven local bank manager, Marisa Bernal was removed without a severance package. Only weeks prior was she presented with a large engraved crystal clock courtesy of Citibank celebrating her banking contributions after 25 years!  What hypocrisy!

asr.full_text: My name is Jay Cronin. I am former secretary of state at University of Los Angeles. As a senator, I have been a lawyer. I have been in the nonprofit system since May, and I have been a minister for two years. One of my favorite things about going to the military was being a good son. I had a really good connection with his mom too, is the personal banker his community, and has been for 25 years. She's the one down in the trenches, the tellers are in the trenches, those are the people bringing in the business, not the upper management. So the upper management has yet once again made a horrible decision. This should be a time where they are concentrating more on bringing more in this thing, rather than getting rid of a manager that's been in for 25 years. loyal, dedicated, honest. And is—even at a time when the Citibank stock was 97 cents she was out there telling everybody, don't worry, everything will be fine. I would definitely consider moving my personal accounts elsewhere if Marissa is not brought back. Because I just do not feel that that is sending the right message to the community, especially, a bank that's received taxpayer dollars. If you were coming into Citibank, it was like your home. If you had anything on your mind, anything to talk about, she would sit there, and be there for you. So it's a piece of a wall that is gone now. She was a lifesaver. She saved my life because the areas of money, my personal account, my credit service, whatever relates to numbers, zero. So she was always there for me when I bought a place for my new office, she was incredible. My son Ken and I have been with Citibank since they moved to Silverlake and we have known Marisa for years and years. And we always said, if she ever leaves we're going with her, what's not to like. Everything. She's very helpful, marvelous personality she's one of those people, to see her gone this morning it's heartbreaking. I was in shock when I found out that she's not there anymore I felt totally, completely abandoned I felt hunger I feel, like you know, she would talk to them in a way that made them feel just as important bringing in their little social security check that month. And you could see that and people sensed that, that she cared about them. Marisa as well as all the tellers and just the general sense of warmth and caring and wonderful customer service and attention to detail, which I always feel comes from the manager. There's no way that exists at a branch if that doesn't come top-down from the manager. If there were too many people in the lines she'd actually come out and be a teller. Because she knew how to do it. One because she knew how to do it and secondly she knew people hated standing in lines and if she could help move them through, that was always really good. I go into the bank now and there's a new person there. I haven't had eye contact, I haven't had hello, how are you, nothing. And not that I even need it on a certain level, but with Marissa. Once you've had it. I know she did a whole lot supporting the new library across the street. And you know, she didn't have to do that. She really believed that the bank should be involved in the community around it, and that's to be admired. It will be proven out that Marissa had loyal followers because of, not just the service, but the quality of her banking services. If ever a case can be made of a huge Wall Street giant beating up on a Main Street hard-working, loyal manager, it's this. I imagine that probably the people at the top didn't even know what was happening. So hopefully they're going to see video and we'll correct it. And if anyone should be fired, it's probably the people who made the absurd decision to fire Marissa.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it presents an interview and testimonial about Marisa Bernal's service as a Citibank manager, her community involvement, and criticism of her removal. The statement about moving personal accounts is framed as a response to the employment dispute, not as a request to invest, pay money, provide credentials, or join a deceptive offer. The described material contains no promoted financial-return claim or connected solicitation.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary subject is general community and employment-related discussion presented through testimonials and criticism about a bank manager's removal and community service.
